kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY VOLCANO ACTIVITY NOTIFICATION
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption, which began at 3:19 a.m. HST on October 17, 2026, continues at 5:00 a.m. HST. The north vent fountain has reached a maximum height of 720 feet (220 m).
kilauea_notices.detail: Episode 55 of lava fountaining in Halemaʻumaʻu began at the summit of Kīlauea began at 3:19 a.m. HST on October 17, 2026 and continues as of this notice. The fountain from the north vent reached a maximum height of just over 700 feet (220 m) by 5:00 a.m. HST. The plume from this eruption is reaching about 25,000 feet above sea level. Winds are blowing from the north-northeast direction, which suggests that volcanic gas emissions and volcanic material may be distributed to the south-southwest direction from Halemaʻumaʻu. Current radar images show significant tephra within the plume up to only 8,000 above sea level. The National Weather Service reports winds above 20,000 feet coming from the west. All eruptive vents and lava flows are confined to Halemaʻumaʻu crater within Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. Tephra fall from volcanic ash clouds is greatest within 3 miles (5 km) of the vents, lighter ash and Pele's Hair may stay suspended for large distances from the vents. Help support science and community awareness by reporting tephra fall: https://hawaiiash.science/report_form Three Kīlauea summit livestream videos that show eruptive lava fountains are available here: https://youtube.com/@usgs/streams KPcam and MKcam provide views of the plume height for aviation purposes Additional short updates as the episode progresses will be posted here: https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/hvo/observatory-messages Timeline of eruptive episodes since December 23, 2024: https://www.usgs.gov/volcanoes/kilauea/science/eruption-information Most lava fountaining episodes since December 23, 2024, have continued for a day or less.

mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
